title: When Low-Code Automation Meets QA Instinct
excerpt: Low-code test automation gets you started fast, but real reliability still comes down to QA instinct: tweaking locators, selectors, and scripts by hand.
html:
Some days in Software QA feel like detective work, and that's actually one of the best parts.

I've been exploring low-code automation in testing, and it's been quite an experience. At first, everything looks simple: record a flow, get suggested locators, and your test is ready.

But as you start relying on those tests more, small challenges begin to show up:

  • A locator that worked yesterday suddenly becomes unreliable
  • A minor UI tweak breaks a test flow
  • Dynamic elements don't behave the same way every time

And that's where I rely more on QA instinct than the tool. I found myself going beyond the "low-code" comfort zone:

  • Tweaking XPath to make it more stable
  • Switching to smarter CSS selectors
  • Adding custom JavaScript when needed
  • Using variables to keep things reusable and clean

It feels less like just running automation and more like solving small, satisfying puzzles every day.

Low-code automation definitely helps speed things up, especially when getting started. But the real value shows up when you start refining, stabilizing, and making those tests truly reliable.

At the end of the day, it's not about how quickly a test is created. It's about how well it holds up over time.
